items.difficulty_reason:
Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 177-180 (book Theorem 3.2.2): it is not the case that every A : \UU satisfies 
eg
eg A 	o A. The statement records only a negative existence claim, while the proof (source lines 181-221) has to build the counterexample from the univalence machinery: it assumes f : \prd{A} (
eg
eg A 	o A), forms the path ua(e) of Bool with itself given by the fixed-point-free swap, applies the dependent action on paths of f at that path, rewrites the result through the transport rule for arrow types (eq:transport-arrow), collapses the transported argument by function extensionality on 
eg
eg Bool, and finally converts the transport along ua(e) in the family A \mapsto A into an application of e, whose fixed-point-freeness is checked by case analysis on Bool. None of these steps is determined by the statement, and no purely propositional manipulation of 
eg
eg A can produce the contradiction.
